_comment: What a WEB build carries: the website and the Android app, which are the same bundle. Each file is an asset of the map-data GitHub Release, pinned by size and sha256, and laid under the build's own assets/ folder at `path`, the stable name the app asks for. scripts/stage-map-assets.mjs downloads and verifies them into map-cache/; `npm run build:web` and `build:site` lay them into dist-web/, and mobile/scripts/stage-www.mjs into the APK's www/. It is the desktop's list (scripts/map-assets.json) cut to what a browser and a phone can hold: the same z8 archives, and the web-sized cut of the world, deep-cleaned like the desktop's (-clean) and with the stock world's owners as country names, built from the seed by scripts/build-default-map.mjs exactly as the desktop's is. Every file must stay under Cloudflare Pages' 25 MiB a file (SITE_FILE_LIMIT_BYTES in the stager; src/runtime/worldFiles.test.js checks it). A browser cannot fetch a release asset itself (GitHub sends no CORS header on the download), which is why the site carries its copy instead of asking for one.
